sentence: This project looks for proteins that change how alpha-synuclein aggregation drives Lewy body disease.
This project tries to find out how a certain molecule affects small cell lung cancer, using mouse models and single cell genomics.
This project runs a lab course that teaches wet-lab methods and basic bioinformatics for single cell analysis.
This project sets up an instrument that measures how strongly immune cells bind to their targets to help test cell therapies for cancer.
This project studies how the immune system responds to gene editing delivered by a virus and tries to calm that response so edited cells last.
This project collects, stores and describes head neck cancer biospecimens for researchers who study the disease.
This project studies how proteins from the host gut stick to Escherichia coli and help it colonize and spread.
This project analyzes genetic, epigenetic and transcriptomic data to learn what chromatin architecture does as tumors start and grow.
This project studies how mutations in a drug target cause resistance, so drugs can be designed to avoid it.
This project tests whether a type of MRI imaging can predict how brain tumors come back and how long patients survive.
This project uses organic synthesis and chemical biology to study small molecules that block a protein in T cells, aiming at autoimmune diseases.
This project studies how Schwann cells in melanoma weaken the immune response against the tumor and tests ways to target those cells.
This project studies genes that may drive systemic sclerosis by analyzing population genetic data and then testing specific immune cells.
This project studies how radiation therapy changes dendritic cells and T-cell responses in pancreatic cancer, using human tissues and mouse models.
This project tests optical genome mapping, a method that uses DNA, as a clinical test to find structural variants in pediatric brain tumors.
This project combines data science, laboratory science and genomic discovery to bring genetic insights into clinical care.
This project studies how breast precancer stem cells escape the immune system and looks for ways to prevent breast cancer.
This project tests whether biomarkers found in the lab can be measured reliably in the clinic for the early detection of lung cancer.
This project studies how endogenous opioids in the brain control motivated behaviors, using opioid specific technologies.
This project studies why lung cancer becomes resistant to a targeted therapy and tries to find ways to overcome that resistance.
